intro: Using Notion for IT project coordinators on Mac helps you keep technical documentation and project timelines in one place. You can manage complex workflows, track sprints, and store meeting notes without leaving your desktop app.
tldr: Use Notion databases to track IT project tasks and dependencies.
Centralize your project briefs, RAID logs, and meeting notes in one workspace.
Use slash commands like /table and /board to build your project hub.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about your screen contents or to find specific buttons.

stats.label: Time spent on work about work

blocks.text: Setting up your Notion workspace for IT projects

Start by creating a master project database. Use the /database command to create a board view. This lets you move tasks through statuses like To Do, In Progress, and Testing. IT projects require clear visibility into dependencies. Add a relation property to link tasks to their parent epics or features. This keeps your hierarchy clean.
Essential Notion tips for IT project coordinators

items: Use templates for recurring meeting notes. Go to the arrow next to New in your database to create a template.
Add a Table of Contents to long technical requirement documents. Type /toc to generate it automatically.
Use callouts for important warnings or project blockers. Type /callout to highlight critical information.
Lock pages that contain final project plans. Click the three dots in the top right and select Lock page.
Use keyboard shortcuts to move faster. Press ⌘ + P to open the search bar and jump between files.

blocks.text: Managing project documentation on your Mac

Documentation is the lifeblood of IT projects. You need to keep your RAID logs, architectural decisions, and sprint retrospectives accessible. Organize these inside a single project page. Use sub-pages for each category to keep the top level clean. If you have external files, embed them directly. Type /embed to bring in Google Sheets or Figma files.

You spend a lot of time typing status updates and meeting summaries. Use the fn key to dictate your notes into Notion. This keeps your hands on the keyboard for navigation while you record thoughts. If you are unsure where a setting is in the Notion interface, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will point to the menu path for you.
Common mistakes to avoid in Notion

items: Creating too many top-level pages instead of using a database hierarchy.
Forgetting to set permissions on sensitive project documents.
Building overly complex formulas that are hard to maintain.
Ignoring the desktop app updates. Always check the Notion menu for the latest version.
Not using the search bar. Use ⌘ + P to find anything in seconds.

blocks.text: Integrating Lazur into your IT workflow

Lazur helps you stay focused on your Mac. When you are in a deep work session, you do not want to hunt through menus. Ask Lazur to guide you through complex steps like creating a new database view. It waits for your input, making the process smooth. Use it to search your calendar or remind you of upcoming project deadlines.

faq.question: What are the system requirements for Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: You need macOS 13 Ventura or later to run the Notion desktop app.

faq.question: How do I find keyboard shortcuts in Notion?
faq.answer: Press Shift + ? on your keyboard while in the Notion app to see the full list.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur explains, points, and guides you, but it does not click buttons or edit your files.
